What you'll do

As BIM Modeler, Civil (Outdoor & Underground), you'll own everything that sits below grade and outside the building line — foundations and equipment pads, electrical duct banks and underground raceway, grounding, and equipment yard layout. On a data center campus this is where the schedule is genuinely won or lost: duct banks have to be right before concrete is poured, and anchor bolts have to match equipment we're already building in our own factory. You'll work in both Revit and AutoCAD, and reconcile Civil 3D surfaces and utility data from our Civil & EPC Lead into the federated model, since translating between these formats is core to the job, not an afterthought. You'll build the outdoor and underground side of our BIM capability rather than maintain someone else's, and be the one person who can say with confidence that this scope is coordinated before anything is poured or shipped.

Where you'll work

We are an in-office culture — velocity matters when you're building physical infrastructure, and the best decisions happen in the room. This role is ideally based in our San Francisco, Long Beach, or Houston offices, with full-time onsite expectations outside of bi-weekly WFH Fridays.

That said, we will make exceptions for truly exceptional talent if you live outside one of our hubs. If you're the right person for this role, we'll have a conversation about what works.

Responsibilities

  • Model foundations, equipment pads, embeds, and anchor bolt setting plans for heavy equipment, coordinated directly against equipment general arrangement drawings
  • Verify anchor bolt and stub-up locations against equipment GAs before pour and before shop release
  • Model electrical duct banks and underground raceway — conduit arrangement, encasement, bend radii, spare capacity, manholes, and pull boxes
  • Model the grounding system — ground grids, rods, conductor routing, and connections to pads, structures, and fence lines
  • Model outdoor structures and equipment yard layout, including electrical clearances, phase spacing, and maintenance access
  • Take in Civil 3D surfaces, utility networks, and survey data and reconcile them into the federated model, including shared coordinates and georeferencing
  • Convert incoming AutoCAD site and utility drawings into native Revit geometry, and produce CAD output back out where required, keeping both in sync
  • Run underground clash cycles in Navisworks — duct bank against foundation, grounding against structure — resolving conflicts rather than just reporting them
  • Build and maintain the parametric Revit family library for repeatable outdoor and underground content — pads, duct bank sections, manholes, and bus supports

We are explicit about this because “outdoor and underground” means different things at different firms. You are not the civil Engineer of Record, and you will not be asked to produce a stamped civil permit set. The following sit with our Civil & EPC Lead and our consultants:

  • Site grading design, earthwork balance, and cut-and-fill authoring in Civil 3D
  • Road corridor design, alignments, and stationing
  • Stormwater sizing, detention basin design, and drainage calculations
  • Civil plan-and-profile sheets and the stamped civil permit set
  • Geotechnical design and bearing capacity
  • Survey and topographic data capture, and legal descriptions
  • Utility interconnection engineering with the serving utility

  • 5+ years modeling foundations, outdoor structures, and underground services for industrial, energy, substation, or mission-critical projects; commercial or residential experience alone will not transfer
  • Expert-level Autodesk Revit, including structural modeling, family creation, parametric content, worksharing, and shared coordinates
  • Strong AutoCAD fluency — genuinely comfortable moving work in both directions between AutoCAD and Revit without losing accuracy
  • Demonstrated experience modeling underground electrical raceway or duct banks, and foundations, equipment pads, or anchor bolt layouts for heavy equipment
  • Able to read, link, and reconcile Civil 3D data — surfaces, pipe networks, alignments, and survey points — into a Revit model
  • Working knowledge of NEC Article 300.5, NESC / IEEE 605, IEEE 80, ASCE 7, ACI 318, and AISC 360
  • Navisworks proficiency, including running clash tests and resolving interference in your own models
  • Authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship

Bonus points

  • Substation civil and structural work — yard layout, equipment foundations, grounding grids, oil containment
  • Hands-on Civil 3D authoring ability

  • Model cable tray, conduit runs, and cable routing for controls systems; coordinate conduit sizing and routing against electrical, mechanical, and structural scopes to avoid conflicts before the build
  • Model control panels, junction boxes, disconnect switches, and cabinet locations to ensure accessibility and proper integration with adjacent systems
  • Convert incoming AutoCAD controls drawings, P&IDs, electrical schematics, and partner controls documentation into native Revit geometry; produce CAD deliverables back out where partners or AHJs require them.

  • Raise and track model change requests so revisions are controlled and stale geometry never reaches a bidder, controls contractor, or site crew
  • Produce controls drawings, system layout plans, instrumentation and I/O location plans, cable routing schedules, conduit and tray schedules, control panel layouts, and sensor/device schedules.
  • Generate model-based quantity takeoffs for cable, conduit, sensors, panels, and controls hardware to support procurement and estimating

  • Familiarity with Template and Modular designs strategies and Processes
  • Contribute to controls model templates, view standards, shared parameters, and naming conventions under the BIM Lead

  • Maintain as-built model updates from field markups, installation photos, and site feedback

  • Able to read and work from P&IDs, electrical schematics, controls system documentation, equipment general arrangements, and sequence of operations

This role works at the center of Giga's People and Finance teams. Payroll execution and controls stay tightly connected to Giga's Controller and accounting team, and benefits direction and the compensation calendar run with People leadership. The reporting home for this role will be confirmed with the selected candidate. Either way, you will own the outcomes below end to end.

In your first 90 days, you will take over the payroll cycle, stabilize the recurring calendar, and document the existing processes, controls, and exceptions. By the end of your first year, Giga should have clean payroll operations, benefits employees understand and use, compensation and equity administration that runs on schedule, and reporting leadership trusts.
